financials_interim.notes: Source: MASK Interim Financial Statements for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (PDF pp.1-10, filed/authorised 12 Aug 2026, cdn.cse.lk/cmt/upload_report_file/723_1786618662400.pdf). Single-entity filing -- only one column of figures is presented (no separate Group/Company split), so per project convention this is entered as a single GROUP row. Operating_profit is NOT an explicit P&L line (structure is Gross Profit -> Other Income -> Change in FV of Biological Assets -> Admin Expenses -> Management Fee -> Finance Cost -> PBT, p.2); derived here as Gross Profit + Other Income - Admin Expenses - Management Fee = 292,361 + 55 - 28,559 - 35,498 = 228,359 (pre-finance-cost operating measure). Short-term borrowings (Rs.370,827k) = the bank overdraft, which the BS classifies under 'Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings' current (p.4) and the cash-flow Note B confirms as the overdraft (p.6); no non-current interest-bearing debt (long_term_borrowings = 0). cash_and_equivalents (Rs.55,044k) is gross Cash & Bank Balances per the BS; net of the Rs.370,827k overdraft the Group's net cash position is actually negative (Rs.(315,783)k per cash-flow Note B, p.6) -- flagged here since the overdraft draw-down is a material driver of the quarter's cash movement. Capex (Rs.11,975k) is 'Purchase of Property, Plant & Equipment' per the cash flow statement; MASK separately discloses 'Field Development Expenditure' of Rs.2,943k (immature-planting capex, not included in the capex field for consistency with the PPE-only convention used elsewhere in this DB) -- both sit inside cash_from_investing (net Rs.(14,734)k). EPS basic 2.87 = PAT 154,618k / 53,953,490 shares in issue -- cross-checked, consistent. No diluted EPS disclosed; eps_diluted left null. Segment note (p.8) discloses four tea estates: Maskeliya, Upcot, Talawakelle, Bandarawela -- Bandarawela's segment gross profit fell 52.4% YoY (Rs.74,377k to Rs.35,416k) on revenue expenditure rising 7.4% (Rs.299,520k to Rs.321,809k) against a 3.3% revenue decline (Rs.389,716k to Rs.376,786k) -- the single largest driver of the Group's 9.2% gross-profit decline. Balance sheet identity check: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity (7,494,025 = 4,371,475 + 3,122,550, exact). PBT - Tax = PAT check: 197,048 - 42,430 = 154,618, exact.

interim_updates.note_text: Maskeliya Plantations PLC (MASK) reported revenue of Rs.1,659.1mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), down 2.5% YoY from Rs.1,702.4mn, and gross profit fell more sharply, down 9.2% YoY to Rs.292.4mn (from Rs.321.9mn). By estate (segment note, p.8), the decline was overwhelmingly concentrated in Bandarawela: segment gross profit fell 52.4% YoY to Rs.35.4mn (from Rs.74.4mn) as revenue expenditure there rose 7.4% (Rs.299,520k to Rs.321,809k) even as segment revenue fell 3.3% (Rs.389,716k to Rs.376,786k) -- Bandarawela alone accounted for a Rs.38,961k swing, more than the Group's entire Rs.29,496k gross-profit decline. Talawakelle partly offset this, with segment gross profit up 28.9% YoY to Rs.96.2mn (from Rs.74.6mn) on lower revenue expenditure (Rs.213,044k to Rs.190,412k) despite flat revenue (Rs.303,218k to Rs.304,940k). Maskeliya estate was broadly stable (gross profit +3.6% to Rs.89.2mn) while Upcot weakened (gross profit -17.6% to Rs.71.5mn from Rs.86.7mn) on lower revenue (Rs.562,848k to Rs.536,603k). Below gross profit, other income collapsed 98.8% YoY to just Rs.55k (from Rs.4,522k) and finance costs rose 13.2% YoY to Rs.31.3mn (from Rs.27.7mn, reflecting a Rs.370,827k bank overdraft drawn during the quarter, versus no overdraft at 31 March 2026) -- both added to the profit decline, though a 13.8% fall in management fee (Rs.41,198k to Rs.35,498k) partly cushioned it. PBT fell 15.5% YoY to Rs.197.0mn (from Rs.233.1mn) and PAT fell 11.7% YoY to Rs.154.6mn (from Rs.175.0mn) as tax expense fell 27.0% YoY (Rs.58.1mn to Rs.42.4mn), partly cushioning the PBT decline; basic EPS fell to Rs.2.87 from Rs.3.24. No specific government/regulatory wage-cost commentary is disclosed for this quarter -- the filing's only labour-cost line is gratuity provision by estate (segment note, p.8), which rose modestly across all four estates (Group total Rs.41,390k to Rs.45,760k, +10.6%) but is not called out as a distinct driver by the company.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for MASK in this database, so no prior quarter (Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) MASK's P&L format has no explicit 'Operating Profit' line -- operating_profit in financial_statements is a derived figure (Gross Profit + Other Income - Admin Expenses - Management Fee), not a number MASK itself discloses; (2) no explanation is given for why Bandarawela's revenue expenditure rose 7.4% against falling revenue (e.g. no mention of a specific cost line, weather event, or wage revision for that estate) -- the segment note gives only revenue/cost/depreciation/gratuity totals with no narrative, so the Bandarawela driver is quantified from the segmental table itself but not independently explained by company commentary; (3) no crop-price or yield commentary (tea auction prices, made-tea kilogram output) is disclosed anywhere in the filing; (4) no government/regulatory wage-cost commentary specific to this quarter, despite gratuity provision rising 10.6% Group-wide -- not called out as a distinct driver by the company.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group gross profit fell 9.2% YoY to Rs.292.4mn almost entirely because of one estate: Bandarawela's segment gross profit collapsed 52.4% (Rs.74.4mn to Rs.35.4mn) as its revenue expenditure rose 7.4% against a 3.3% revenue decline -- a swing (Rs.38.96mn) larger than the Group's entire gross-profit decline (Rs.29.5mn). Talawakelle partly offset this (+28.9% to Rs.96.2mn on lower cost), but PBT still fell 15.5% YoY to Rs.197.0mn as other income evaporated (-98.8% to Rs.55k) and finance costs rose 13.2% on a newly drawn Rs.370.8mn bank overdraft. PAT fell a smaller 11.7% to Rs.154.6mn only because tax expense fell 27.0% YoY.
operational_highlights: Revenue down 2.5% YoY to Rs.1,659.1mn (from Rs.1,702.4mn); gross profit down 9.2% YoY to Rs.292.4mn (from Rs.321.9mn)

Bandarawela estate segment gross profit fell 52.4% YoY to Rs.35.4mn (from Rs.74.4mn, segment note p.8) as revenue expenditure rose 7.4% (Rs.299,520k to Rs.321,809k) against a 3.3% revenue decline (Rs.389,716k to Rs.376,786k) -- the single largest driver of the Group's gross-profit decline
Talawakelle estate segment gross profit rose 28.9% YoY to Rs.96.2mn (from Rs.74.6mn) on lower revenue expenditure (Rs.213,044k to Rs.190,412k) despite flat revenue -- partly offsetting Bandarawela
Upcot estate segment gross profit fell 17.6% YoY to Rs.71.5mn (from Rs.86.7mn) on lower revenue (Rs.562,848k to Rs.536,603k); Maskeliya estate broadly stable (+3.6% to Rs.89.2mn)
Other income fell 98.8% YoY to Rs.55k (from Rs.4,522k) -- a small absolute drag on PBT

Finance costs up 13.2% YoY to Rs.31.3mn (from Rs.27.7mn), reflecting a Rs.370,827k bank overdraft drawn during the quarter (nil at 31 March 2026) -- net cash position swung to Rs.(315,783)k from Rs.55,044k gross cash
PBT down 15.5% YoY to Rs.197.0mn; tax expense down 27.0% YoY to Rs.42.4mn cushioned the PAT decline to 11.7% YoY (Rs.175.0mn to Rs.154.6mn); basic EPS Rs.2.87 (from Rs.3.24)

Net cash used in operating activities was Rs.(350,539)k (from Rs.36,063k generated a year earlier), driven by a Rs.475,285k increase in inventories (tea stock build) versus a Rs.185,922k increase a year earlier
key_drivers: Bandarawela estate segment gross profit -52.4% YoY (Rs.74,377k to Rs.35,416k, segment note p.8) on a 7.4% rise in revenue expenditure against a 3.3% revenue decline -- the single largest driver of the Group's 9.2% gross-profit decline and of the PBT decline
Talawakelle estate segment gross profit +28.9% YoY (Rs.74,647k to Rs.96,238k) on lower revenue expenditure -- the main offsetting driver

Other income -98.8% YoY (Rs.4,522k to Rs.55k) and finance costs +13.2% YoY (Rs.27,662k to Rs.31,311k, on a newly drawn Rs.370,827k overdraft) together account for most of the gap between the 9.2% gross-profit decline and the larger 15.5% PBT decline
Tax expense -27.0% YoY (Rs.58,106k to Rs.42,430k) was the main reason PAT fell a smaller 11.7% than PBT's 15.5% decline
